sentences.scope: Found in the email of 4 employees, December 1999 to March 2002.
sentences.split: About a quarter is email time counted from the messages; most is hands-on work estimated from them.
sentences.range: The estimates put it between $1,243 and $4,989.
sentences.today: This work costs $5,277 a month today (62.1 hours); the $2,231 is the part that could be automated. Both are floors: email shows only part of the work.
sentences.concentration: About a third of the processes in the total (16 of 42, worth $1,359 of the $2,231) draw 90% or more of their messages from one mailbox.
sentences.caution: 3 of the 5 processes with documents come almost only from one person’s mailbox. Read each finding as what one person’s mail shows.
sentences.threshold: We draft a working document for every process seen 10 or more times over 3 or more months by 2 or more staff whose automatable work is worth one hour a month ($85) or more.
sentences.sensitivity: 3 processes clear it with every estimate at its low end, 5 at the middle, 17 at the high end.
sentences.averaging: Each process is averaged over the time it was seen, from its first email to its last: one seen over 7.9 months counts as 7.9 months of work, not the 28 months the archive spans.
sentences.not_included: 18 processes seen too rarely to count ($452 a month), and 115 messages that fit no recurring process. Personal mail, newsletters, system notices and duplicates are read and set aside.
sentences.no_reply: There is no later message in these mailboxes; the answer may have come by phone or in mail we do not have.
sentences.reading: $214 of the counted part is reading time: one published minute per staff addressee, half of it automatable.

findings.stall_summary: Schedule sheets repeatedly carry errors that have to be reworked: duplicate schedules, wrong lending positions and missing schedules in the EPE sheet.

quote.raw_text: Friday's sheet for Monday had a duplicate 10 mw schedule in it

findings.fix: Generate the preschedule and EPE schedule sheets from the deals booked in Enpower, with checks that flag duplicate schedules, lending volumes that differ from the deal, and import IDs or tags that do not match the CISO submission.

findings.stall_summary: Requesters wait on replies and chase repeatedly for status on a meter, sometimes after voicemails, and one escalates in capitals asking for anyone to help resolve the matter.

quote.raw_text: Anita, have you found out any further information about this meter.

findings.fix: A daily exception report that matches measured meter flow against deals and nominations and lists each meter, day and volume with no deal, with the last deal at that meter and its trader attached.

findings.stall_summary: Settlements waits on the scheduler or trader to verify deals, chasing with follow-ups while payment dates approach.

quote.raw_text: we are waiting on a response from Daren

findings.fix: Run a daily match of counterparty invoices against Sitara deal prices and volumes, listing each variance with deal number, both figures, the responsible desk and the payment due date, and send it to the owning scheduler or trader with a standard query.
